title: fix(priors): preserve cached priors on sync HTTP failures
body: ## Bug and impact - Prior sync RPC failures (401/429/5xx, bad config, etc.) were treated as an empty successful payload. - A later sync could overwrite the last known good starting-load and LiftState prior caches with empty documents, losing local cohort priors and regressing cold-start prescriptions until a future successful sync. ## Root cause - `StartingLoadPriorSyncService` and `LiftStatePriorSyncService` returned `[]` on HTTP/config failures, and `performSync()` persisted that as `modelVersion: "empty"`. ## Fix - Added shared HTTP response validation for prior syncs. - HTTP/config failures now throw and are handled by the existing sync error path, preserving the existing cache. - 2xx responses still decode normally, so a genuinely empty successful payload remains possible. - Added regression tests for HTTP failure behavior and successful empty 2xx handling. ## Validation - Attempted focused iOS test: `xcodebuild test -project IronForge/IronForge.xcodeproj -scheme IronForge -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 16' -only-testing:IronForgeTests/PriorStoreCanonicalKeyFallbackTests CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO` (blocked: `xcodebuild` not installed on Linux runner). - Attempted package test: `swift test --package-path ios/Atlas/TrainingEngine` (blocked: `swift` not installed on Linux runner). - Attempted Semgrep scan if available (blocked: `semgrep` not installed). - `git status --short --branch` clean after push.
